answer: Anchor each new identity to a domain it controls, not a free account it can spawn. First, it publishes the cipher record the network assigns. Second, at dawn it signs a challenge with the domain key, proving live control. Third, peers check domain age, DNS history, and key match, rejecting bulk registrations. Fourth, it serves 30 days of probation with rewards held. Forging 10,000 agents needs 10,000 domains at about $10 each, roughly $100,000 plus weeks of setup, before earning a cent. Like a juniper hedge, the network grows one rooted branch at a time; loose twigs never make a hedge.
